demographics.chief_complaint: Acute dyspnea, high fever, productive cough

clinical_scenario: Community-Acquired Bacterial Pneumonia with Severe Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure

raw_inputs.ehr: Patient is a 68-year-old male with a history of hypertension and mild COPD who presents to the emergency department with acute onset of fever (102.4°F), chills, and productive cough with rust-colored sputum for 4 days. Dyspnea worsened significantly this morning. Labs: WBC 16.2 x10^3/uL (86% neutrophils, 8% bands). Procalcitonin elevated at 2.4 ng/mL. Serum lactate: 2.1 mmol/L.

demographics.chief_complaint: Sudden pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath after 14-hour flight

clinical_scenario: Acute Pulmonary Embolism (Conflict / Debate Case: Clear CXR with profound hypoxia and sinus tachycardia)

raw_inputs.ehr: 54-year-old female presents with sudden sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain and breathlessness. Returned from international flight 48 hours ago. Past medical history: Oral contraceptive use, mild obesity. D-dimer markedly elevated at 3,200 ng/mL FEU. Troponin T mildly elevated at 0.04 ng/mL.

demographics.chief_complaint: Increased wheezing and increased inhaler usage for 3 days

clinical_scenario: Moderate Acute Exacerbation of COPD without Acute Pneumonia

raw_inputs.ehr: 72-year-old male with 45 pack-year smoking history and Gold Stage II COPD reports increased cough, clear sputum volume, and expiratory wheezing triggered by seasonal cold. Has been using albuterol every 2 hours with partial relief. Afebrile. WBC 9.1 x10^3/uL (normal). CRP mildly elevated at 8 mg/L.

demographics.chief_complaint: Mild viral upper respiratory symptoms and dry cough

raw_inputs.ehr: 29-year-old healthy female with 2-day history of scratchy throat, nasal congestion, and mild non-productive cough. No dyspnea, no chest pain. Denies known sick contacts. Vitals stable. Physical exam reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally with no crackles or wheezes.
